title: Hybrid Intelligent Decision-Support Architecture for Explainable Adaptation of Collaborative Learning Scripts: A Simulation Benchmark
content: Collaborative learning scripts are mainly fixed, and collaboration dashboards do not directly trigger teachers to intervene. We thus introduce a hybrid intelligent decision-support system and a simulation benchmark with introduced group dysfunctions, known onsets and a true per-group oracle. The system includes quantile-anchored fuzzy inference (35 rules), a lexical content classifier, calibrated gradient-boosting detectors with 3-levels explanations, expected-benefit selection from a closed operator catalogue, and NSGA-II regrouping. Teacher approval is designed, but was not evaluated. After 20 simulated datasets, the detectors achieved macro-F1=0.591, macro-AUROC=0.870 and isotonic calibration reduced expected calibration error to 0.018-0.025. The fuzzy indicators were practically indistinguishable from no indicators in accuracy (posterior probability of a difference within ±0.01: 0.96); the intended value of traceable rule-level evidence is yet to be tested with teachers. Generalisation was main limitation: under changed mechanism, macro-F1 fell from 0.586 to 0.297; in a held-out topic, the full model fell below the interaction-only model (0.402 versus 0.437); in new paraphrases, misconception F1 dropped to 0.146. SHAP explanations came close to occlusion and interventional SHAP explanations and greatly surpassed a model-free ranking, but the detector dependent on construct irrelevant features so verbalisations had to be post-filtered by a consistency predicate. At the operating point determined on training data, operator selection was 0.399 of the oracle's harm-mitigation with 18.7% undesired interventions, matching a fixed operator map. Class-level regrouping increased simulated harm; greedy-seeded NSGA-II was only slightly better than other greedy-seeded searches. These simulation results must be regarded as upper bounds.
